q:

II) If the bearing is opening away from the bow so the buoy is moving aft relative to the reference point, then the ship’s distance from the buoy is increasing. If the rate at which the buoy is opening is increasing then the rate of turn is decreasing
III) Using a buoy in this manner is especially effective when turning in a strong current
IV) The angle between the lines of buoys marking the port and starboard sides of a channel can be used with great accuracy both to predict the ship’s future position in a reach into which she is turning, and to know the vessel’s position relative to the centerline after she has steadied up in that reach
opts: All are true
Only I, II and III are true
Only I, II and IV are true
Only II, III and IV are true
Only II is true

q: According to Shiphandling for the Mariner, in the portion of a river where the channel narrows, the ship begins feeling the steep bank close on the starboard hand. If the ship gets so close to the bank that she starts to sheer across the channel, the best maneuvers to do are:
opts: Reduce engine speed; Let the head fall a few degrees off course across the channel while maintaining some rudder angle toward the near bank; Increase engine speed; When the heading has changed a few degrees toward the center of the channel, increase rudder angle toward the near bank to first check that swing and then to bring the ship back on course as she reaches the center of the channel

Reduce engine speed; Let the head fall a few degrees off course across the channel while maintaining some rudder angle toward the near bank; When the heading has changed a few degrees toward the center of the channel, increase rudder angle toward the farthest bank to first check that swing and then to bring the ship back on course as she reaches the center of the channel

Don’t reduce engine speed; Let the head fall a few degrees off course across the channel while maintaining some rudder angle toward the near bank; Increase engine speed; When the heading has changed a few degrees toward the center of the channel, increase rudder angle toward the farthest bank to first check that swing and then to bring the ship back on course as she reaches the center of the channel

Don’t reduce engine speed; Let the head fall a few degrees off course across the channel while maintaining some rudder angle toward the near bank; Increase engine speed; When the heading has changed a few degrees toward the center of the channel, increase rudder angle toward the near bank to first check that swing and then to bring the ship back on course as she reaches the center of the channel
